result.summary: Escapes embedded newline characters as '\x0a' in the logging subsystem via BCLog::LogEscapeMessage. Strips any single trailing newline from log messages before escaping and appends the final newline centrally in Logger::Format. Adds functional tests verifying that newlines in rejected RPC method names and wallet paths cannot forge new log lines in debug.log.
result.problem: Untrusted user inputs like rejected RPC method names or wallet names can contain unescaped newline characters. Restricted RPC users or callers can exploit this to inject forged log entries into debug.log, potentially misleading node operators or automated log monitoring tools.
evidence: PR description provides a concrete reproducer where an unauthorized RPC call to 'getblock\n<fake error>' successfully injects an 'ERROR: ConnectTip: ConnectBlock ... failed' line into debug.log
result.changed_since_previous: Dropped the util::SplitLines helper and the updates across multiline logging call sites (exceptions, UI messages, wallet diagnostics), keeping only the core logger escaping change and functional tests.
result.card: This pull request prevents user inputs from forging log lines in debug.log by escaping embedded newlines as hex sequences in the logging subsystem. Currently, inputs such as rejected RPC method names or wallet paths preserve newlines through log escaping, allowing restricted RPC users to inject fake entries that appear to come from the node. The author demonstrates this with a reproducer injecting a fake block connection error into debug.log. Trailing newlines from existing log calls are stripped before escaping and re-appended centrally to avoid altering normal single-line formatting.

risk.why: A flaw in log message formatting could corrupt debug.log readability or break external tools that parse log outputs.
